title: Okeh songs handed to her at sessions; "Mourning Dove Blues"
summary: She sang songs given her at the Okeh office without practice and discusses 1925 sessions with Joe Oliver and Herschel and which tunes she wrote.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: They ran me in there. The man (unintelligible). This was money to (unintelligible) like you owe
me some and wanted me to sing, and he would give me (unintelligible).
I see. The man who wrote the songs?
When you went to the O.K. office, is that it?
Oh, so you saw the songs for the first time when you went to record? You didn't practice it? Did you practice it?
Did you read music? Did you know how to read music?
Not too good. But see, I sing music and I wasn't going to play it, no how. It was (unintelligible) played, he'd play and I'd sing it down the road and (unintelligible).
Now here, for example, in February 1925, Joe Oliver was playing for you, playing coronet, and your brother Herschel was playing the piano?
"Mourning Dove Blues." I made a big hit, too.
Yeah. "Devil Dance Blues", "Every Dog Has Its Day".
Now, you remember who wrote those songs?
Now, in a case like that, would somebody -- would another song writer put the money on for the song, either of those two, like "Every Dog has His Day" or "Mourning Dove Blues"?
See, you remember, "Every Dog Has His Day", I wrote that, too.
